room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
hook: "may-REE": a bride and groom who have just come to MARRY at the TOWN HALL cut their wedding cake: MARRY
note: La mairie is the town hall of a commune; in France every civil wedding takes place there, in front of the mayor.

room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
change: added (street verb rehomed per the verbplan mairie rows; Monsieur Verbe, red beret); vocab room ST_social_seg002 -> R_politics_01
hook: "ah-kor-DAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret), an ACCORDION strapped to his chest, GRANTS the newlyweds the big gold key of the town, tied with a red bow: A-CORD-AY: ACCORDION
note: Accorder means to grant or to give (accorder une faveur, accorder dix minutes); it also means to tune an instrument (accorder un piano). S'accorder: to agree, or to go well together (des couleurs qui s'accordent).

room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
hook: "mee-NEESTR": a stately MINISTER in a dark suit sips punch through a teeny MINI STRAW from a tall punch glass: MINI-STRAW
note: Un ministre heads a government department; the word is masculine or feminine (le/la ministre). Not a church minister: that is un pasteur.

room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
hook: "pray-zee-DAHN": everyone PRAISES DON, the club PRESIDENT, who blushes and lifts a gold trophy cup over his head: PRAISE-E-DON
note: Président also means the chair of a club, a meeting or a company (le président du club).

room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
hook: "day-pew-TAY": a DEPUTY in a suit with a tricolor sash taps a golf PUTT across the parquet toward a little golf hole on a green felt mat: DAY-PUTT-AY
note: Un député is an elected member of the Assemblée nationale (a member of Parliament, like a U.S. representative), not a sheriff's deputy.

room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
hook: "mee-nees-TEHR": on a round table stands a big model of the MINISTRY, and a little boy walks two fingers up its MINI STAIRcase: MINI-STAIR
note: Un ministère is a government department and its building (le ministère de la Culture).

room_name: Le salon d'honneur · The reception hall
hook: "kohn-GREH": a waiter brings a tray of GRAY ice-cream CONES to the CONGRESS delegates, who stare at the strange gray scoops: CONE-GRAY
note: Un congrès is a large formal meeting or conference (un congrès de médecins); in the U.S., le Congrès is Congress.

room_name: Le bureau des papiers · The paperwork office
hook: "see-nyah-TEWR": a TOUR guide holding up a little yellow pennant signs her name with a big swirly SIGNATURE while her tourists in sun hats wave 'SEE YA!': SEE-YA-TOUR
note: La signature is both your signature and the act of signing (la signature du contrat).

room_name: Le bureau des papiers · The paperwork office
hook: "day-MAHRSH": a man with an armful of forms MARCHES like a drum major from counter to counter, knees high: the long DÉMARCHE (process): DAY-MARCH
note: Also means a person's walk or gait (une démarche élégante) and a step taken to get something done (faire des démarches).

room_name: Le bureau des papiers · The paperwork office
hook: "doh-SYAY": a young DOE pokes her head over the counter and nibbles the corner of a fat DOSSIER (file) a clerk holds out: DOE-SEE-AY
note: Second sense: the back of a chair (le dossier de la chaise).

room_name: Le bureau des papiers · The paperwork office
hook: "SOH": a gray-haired lady SEWS a red ribbon onto the document while the clerk beside her presses a brass SEAL into a blob of red wax on it: SEW
note: Same sound as seau (bucket), saut (jump) and sot (fool): only the spelling sceau means seal.

room_name: Le bureau des papiers · The paperwork office
hook: "doh-kew-MAHN": a DOCtor in a white coat points with a billiard CUE at the notice board where the important DOCUMENTs go: DOC-CUE-MAN
note: Like English document; also a computer file (un document Word).

room_name: Le bureau des papiers · The paperwork office
hook: "pehr-MEE": a freckled teenage boy with a fresh curly red PERM, still in pink rollers, proudly holds up his new driver's PERMIT: PERM-ME
note: Le permis de conduire is a driver's license; un permis de construire is a building permit.

room_name: La salle des élections · The polling hall
hook: "pahn-KAHRT": a cook pushes a CART full of shiny frying PANS, and a big blank PLACARD on a pole sticks up out of it: PAN-CART
note: Une pancarte is any sign or placard: a notice on a door or a sign carried in a march.

room_name: La salle des élections · The polling hall
hook: "bahn-duh-ROL": a little marching BAND plays under the long blank BANNER they have just unROLLed across the hall: BAND-A-ROLL
note: Une banderole is a long banner carried in a march or hung up at a match.

room_name: La salle des élections · The polling hall
change: added (street verb rehomed per the verbplan mairie rows; Monsieur Verbe, red beret); vocab room ST_rule_seg004 -> R_politics_03
hook: "voh-TAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) VOTES, dropping his envelope into the clear ballot box while balancing a cup of TEA on its saucer in his other hand: VOTE-TEA
note: Voter pour quelqu'un = to vote for someone. Une voix is a vote cast.

room_name: La salle des élections · The polling hall
hook: "pahr-tee-ZAHN": a cheering SUPPORTER waves a giant wedge of PARMESAN cheese over his head like a foam finger: PARMESAN
note: Un partisan is a supporter of an idea or a person (un partisan du vélo). It is not party-political in the English sense of 'partisan'; in history it also means a resistance fighter.

room_name: La salle des élections · The polling hall
hook: "ay-lehk-TUHR": an elderly VOTER in line gives A LECTURE to a bored teenager, wagging a finger, ballot envelope in hand: A-LECTURE
note: Une électrice is a woman voter. La carte d'électeur is the voter card.

room_name: La salle des élections · The polling hall
hook: "ay-LEW": two friends lift LOU, the newly ELECTED official, onto their shoulders, and the crowd shouts 'HEY, LOU!': HEY-LOU
note: Un élu is any elected official (les élus municipaux); as an adjective, élu means elected or chosen.

room_name: La salle des fêtes · The village hall
hook: "peh-YAHN": at the door a visitor PAYS for his ticket and the cashier gives an enormous YAWN: entry is PAYANT (not free): PAY-YAWN
note: Payant means you have to pay (le parking est payant); the opposite is gratuit, free. Of a job or business: paying, profitable.

room_name: La salle des fêtes · The village hall
hook: "rahn-TAHBL": a beekeeper lady pays to RENT A TABLE at the fair and stacks it with honey jars that sell fast: PROFITABLE: RENT-A-TABLE
note: Rentable means profitable or worth it (un investissement rentable); it comes from la rente, income, not from English 'rent'.

room_name: La salle des fêtes · The village hall
hook: "bay-nay-VOL": BENNY, a VOLUNTEER in a green apron, keeps a beach ball going in a VOLLEY with the children, unpaid and happy: BENNY-VOLLEY
note: Also a noun: un or une bénévole is a volunteer (unpaid helper).

room_name: La salle des fêtes · The village hall
hook: "fyeh-ruh-MAHN": a FIREMAN in his shiny helmet stands PROUDLY with his chest out and a new medal on his jacket: FIRE-MAN
note: Fièrement comes from fier, proud (fier de son travail).

room_name: La salle des fêtes · The village hall
hook: "pay-zee-bluh-MAHN": an old man in a PAISLEY BLUE shirt dozes PEACEFULLY in a folding chair up on the stage: PAISLEY-BLUE-MAN
note: Paisiblement comes from paisible, peaceful (from la paix, peace).

room_name: La salle des fêtes · The village hall
hook: "kah-ray-MAHN": a strongman CARRIES a whole upright piano across the hall in his arms: carrément, really, the WHOLE thing!: CARRY-MAN
note: Carrément is informal: 'totally, really' (c'est carrément génial) or 'bluntly, straight out' (il me l'a dit carrément).
